te: Solving the stray dog problem from start to finish: upstream, midstream and downstream
se: The meeting considered the stray dog problem, which affects safety, hygiene and rabies control, and proposed a complete management model. It starts upstream by preventing the abandonment of animals and building owners' responsibility through the law and public education, and goes on to the care of animals already on the streets, aiming at "disease-free animals, safe people"
it: A systematic approach to the stray dog problem (upstream, midstream, downstream)

te: Shrimp output down by more than half: a "support–control–market" approach proposed
se: The meeting considered the situation of the Thai shrimp industry, whose output has fallen by more than 50 per cent compared with 10 years ago because of erratic weather, the environment and diseases in aquatic animals, while costs are high, especially electricity at about 35 per cent of costs, and Thailand is at a tariff disadvantage in the European Union market. The meeting proposed a recovery approach under the idea of "support–control–market"
it: Situation of the Thai shrimp industry and ways to revive it

te: Ways sought to revive the Thai shrimp industry and cope with erratic water conditions
se: The meeting considered measures to solve the problems of the Thai shrimp industry, following the requests of shrimp farmers, to restore output and increase competitiveness in the world market. It proposed that farmers move to high-efficiency farms that use data and real-time water quality technology, to reduce the risks from erratic weather and disease
it: Measures to solve problems in and revive the Thai shrimp industry

te: First meeting: framework set for livestock and fisheries work, animal epidemics and the stray dog problem
se: At its first meeting after the committee appointed the subcommittee, the meeting discussed the new strain of foot-and-mouth disease spreading abroad and the Department of Livestock Development's preparations; opportunities to export livestock products to Singapore and Malaysia, which require higher farm standards; and the problem of stray dogs and rabies, proposing serious use of the catch–neuter–vaccinate–return (CNVR) approach. The scope of work covers everything from production to marketing
it: Order appointing the subcommittee and its framework for work noted
The animal epidemic situation and opportunities to export livestock products
The problem of stray dogs and rabies

te: Meeting 12/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Integrated Agricultural Networks to International Standards for the Environment and Sustainability
Meeting 11/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Integrated Agricultural Networks to International Standards for the Environment and Sustainability
Meeting 11/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Integrated Agricultural Networks to International Standards for the Environment and Sustainability
Model for an integrated value-added agro-industrial zone considered
se: The meeting considered the organisational structure and management mechanism for an integrated value-added agro-industrial zone, which aims to link farmers' production from upstream to downstream in one area, in order to cut costs, produce what the market wants, add value through processing and help solve farmers' debt problems, in cooperation with the agencies concerned
it: Organisational structure and management mechanism for an integrated value-added agro-industrial zone

te: Summary of the Chon Buri and Rayong visits, and the structure of the agro-industrial zone considered
se: The meeting noted the summary of the study visit on farming systems and integrated agricultural processing industries in Chon Buri and Rayong Provinces on 2–4 September 2026. It observed that farmers still find it hard to obtain machinery because of high costs, and felt the state should provide machinery for rent at suitable rates. It also considered the structure and management mechanism of an integrated value-added agro-industrial zone, and felt that a specific law should be considered so that the work can continue
it: Summary of the study visit to Chon Buri and Rayong Provinces, 2–4 September 2026
Organisational structure and management mechanism for an integrated value-added agro-industrial zone

te: Meeting 8/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Integrated Agricultural Networks to International Standards for the Environment and Sustainability
Briefing by NSTDA and NRCT on agricultural technology and research
se: The meeting studied agricultural technology and innovation to increase efficiency, cut costs and add value to products. It invited the President of the National Science and Technology Development Agency and the Director of the National Research Council of Thailand to give information on research ready for use, such as precision irrigation systems and growing legumes to improve the soil. There were also proposals to develop research staff, provide suitable research funding and integrate cooperation between the public and private sectors

te: Briefing by community enterprises that apply "market-led production"
se: The meeting heard representatives of 2 community enterprises describe how farmers grouped together to grow crops to meet market demand under GAP standards, which gives members stable prices and incomes. The meeting felt this information is useful for setting up an integrated agricultural estate, and there were proposals such as raising standards and improving the certification system, setting land use to suit each area's potential, and creating incentives by sharing benefits with participating farmers
it: Experience of community enterprises with market-led production
Proposals on product standards, land use and benefit-sharing with farmers

te: Briefing on state property land, agricultural markets and exports
se: The meeting studied the suitability of areas and the use of farmland in line with the market. It invited a representative of the Treasury Department to explain the rules for using state property land, a representative of the Department of Internal Trade to explain the structure of agricultural products and measures on sales channels, such as central agricultural markets and auction market systems, and a representative of the Department of Foreign Trade to explain approaches to promoting agricultural exports
it: Rules for requesting the use of state property land for an integrated agricultural estate
Structure of agricultural products and sales channels

te: Briefing by water agencies to support setting up an integrated agricultural estate
se: The meeting studied water resource management to support the setting up of an integrated agricultural estate. It invited representatives of the Land Development Department, the Royal Irrigation Department and the Department of Groundwater Resources to explain the country's water situation, the potential for developing water sources and related plans, such as building on-farm water sources outside irrigation zones and managing soil and water in drought-risk areas
it: Water situation, water source development potential and related plans for agriculture

te: Foreign approaches and laws on agricultural development studied
se: The meeting studied approaches, models and principles for developing an integrated agricultural sector, including Taiwan's agricultural development law, which sets up a system covering resource management, risk reduction, stable incomes, higher production standards and an estate management body that serves operators, as background for developing Thai agriculture
it: Approaches, models and principles for developing an integrated agricultural sector
Taiwan's agricultural development law and model

te: Farmers' problems and the role of integrated agricultural estates studied
se: The meeting studied examples of integrated farming systems and agro-industrial estates, starting from farmers' long-standing problems, such as high costs, low yields per rai, uneven quality, low prices imposed by buyers, selling only fresh produce, and difficult access to foreign markets. It then considered how an integrated agricultural estate could solve these problems systematically
it: Farmers' problems and the mechanisms of an integrated agricultural estate that may help solve them
